findings.text: Total 6 incidents logged over 7 months from 2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23: 4 with dumps (Bugcheck 307 x3 and 278 x1) and 2 freezes without dump (Bugcheck 0x0)
All 4 dumps blame the same module nvlddmkm.sys (NVIDIA kernel graphics driver)

Same failure CATEGORY recurrence: incidents inc-001, inc-003, inc-004 share identical FAILURE_BUCKET_ID and hash indicating same failure category (DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION ISR timeout). This does not alone prove same root defect as any other machine, only internal consistency
Incident inc-006 is a different category but still same module nvlddmkm.sys with VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0x116) - consistent with graphics timeout family

Failure persists across driver versions: nvlddmkm.sys blamed with 2 distinct driver timestamps 2026-03-04 (inc-003, inc-004) and 2026-02-14 (inc-006), plus an undated driver in inc-001. This is the strongest argument to escalate to the manufacturer - driver update alone did not resolve
Repetition threshold met: 4 incidents within 90 days 2026-04-22..2026-07-21 - indicates chronic instability not isolated spike

manufacturer_report.body_en:
Device: Lenovo with NVIDIA GPU
Model: Lenovo (NVIDIA GPU) - Serial: {{SERIAL}}
Purchase date: 2026-01

Incident timeline (timezone America/Managua): 6 incidents logged from 2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23. Breakdown: 4 incidents with minidumps (Bugcheck 307 x3 = 0x133 and Bugcheck 278 x1 = 0x116) and 2 freezes without dump (Bugcheck 0x0 - inc-002, inc-005). Repetition: 4 incidents within 90 days 2026-04-22..2026-07-21 indicating chronic instability.

Error codes and analysis:
- 0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (parameter 0x1, 0x1e00) ISR timeout: inc-001, inc-003, inc-004 share identical FAILURE_BUCKET_ID "0x133_ISR_nvlddmkm!unknown_function" and FAILURE_ID_HASH "{f97493a5-ea2b-23ca-a808-8602773c2a86}" indicating same failure category internally. This does not alone prove same defect as other machines, only internal consistency.
- 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0xc000009a): inc-006 with FAILURE_BUCKET_ID "0x116_IMAGE_nvlddmkm.sys" and hash "{c89bfe8c-ed39-f658-ef27-f2898997fdbd}" - different category but same module and graphics timeout family.
- 2 freezes without dump: Bugcheck 0x0.

Responsible module: nvlddmkm.sys (NVIDIA kernel graphics driver) - 4/4 dumps_with_common_module.

Driver versions:
- Timestamp 2026-03-04 in inc-003, inc-004
- Timestamp 2026-02-14 in inc-006
- Undated driver in inc-001
Failure persists across at least 2 driver versions.

Power transition context:
- 3 of 6 incidents occurred during power transition (SleepInProgress !=0): inc-002 (4), inc-003 (1), inc-005 (4)
- 3 incidents with SleepInProgress 0: inc-001, inc-004, inc-006 (active use)
Hypothesis under investigation: sleep/wake triggers may expose GPU hang, but hang also occurs in normal use, pointing away from pure power-management software bug toward hardware/firmware or low-level driver timing.

OS health logs:
- disk: No disk errors logged
- hardware: No WHEA memory or CPU errors logged
- thermal (CPU): No CPU throttling due to temperature logged
- software: No repeated application failures logged
These playbooks are clean but are limited to OS-visible logs.

Steps already taken:
- Driver updates applied (evidence shows at least two different driver timestamps) - issue recurred
- OS logs reviewed, no alternative cause found

Request:
Please perform comprehensive GPU diagnosis: confirm VBIOS version, check GPU/VRAM temperature, hotspot and fan speed logs, verify PSU and PCIe power rails, run VRAM and GPU stress tests (FurMark/OCCT), PCIe reseat test, and test with Lenovo-recommended NVIDIA driver branch (Studio vs GameReady) and latest BIOS. If hardware fault, firmware incompatibility, or systemic driver family defect is confirmed, please advise on warranty repair/replacement procedure. Missing data (thermal logs, PSU logs, BIOS version, full driver history, kernel dumps) will be provided on request.

findings.text: System recorded 6 incidents total from 2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23 (7 months span): 4 with bugcheck dumps and 2 freezes without dump (BugcheckCode 0x0)
Repetition threshold met: 4 incidents within 90 days (2026-04-22 .. 2026-07-21)
All 4 available dumps implicate the same module nvlddmkm.sys

3 of 4 dumps share identical Failure Category: bugcheck 0x133 (DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION, 0x133_ISR_nvlddmkm!unknown_function) with Failure ID Hash {f97493a5-ea2b-23ca-a808-8602773c2a86}. Per rule, same hash means same failure CATEGORY only, not proof of same underlying defect as other machines

1 dump is a different Failure Category: 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0x116_IMAGE_nvlddmkm.sys) with Failure ID Hash {c89bfe8c-ed39-f658-ef27-f2898997fdbd} - still same module nvlddmkm.sys but differing bugcheck code

Failure persists across driver versions: nvlddmkm.sys failed with 2 distinct driver timestamps (2026-02-14 and 2026-03-04). This is the strongest argument to escalate to the manufacturer, as it is not isolated to a single driver build
Inc-001 (2026-04-22) also implicates nvlddmkm.sys with same 0x133 category but driver_timestamp is null/null in precomputed data - cannot be counted toward distinct version count
Two bugcheck codes observed, both GPU stack related: 0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (x3 dumped) and 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (x1) + 2 additional 0x0 NO_BLUE_SCREEN freezes
3 of 6 incidents occurred during power transition (SleepInProgress = 1 or 4: inc-002, inc-003, inc-005), suggesting possible correlation with sleep/wake/power management, but sample size is small

Root cause is likely GPU hardware/firmware/power-delivery interaction or deep driver-OS compatibility issue rather than single buggy driver install, because same module fails across multiple driver versions and multiple bugcheck categories. Cannot distinguish hardware defect vs firmware vs power without further testing
